domain_hypothesis.reasoning: The dataset contains columns related to employee demographics (Age, Gender, MaritalStatus), job characteristics (JobRole, Department, JobLevel, JobSatisfaction), compensation (MonthlyIncome, PercentSalaryHike, StockOptionLevel), and attrition (Attrition). These signals strongly indicate a human resources domain focused on employee retention and workforce analytics.

kpi_specs.name: Attrition Rate
kpi_specs.description: Percentage of employees who have left the company (Attrition = 'Yes'). This KPI is critical for assessing workforce stability and retention efforts.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(*)) * 100 AS attrition_rate FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: Attrition rate is a fundamental HR KPI for retention analysis. A single summary number is best displayed as a card for quick insight.

kpi_specs.name: Attrition by Department
kpi_specs.description: Breakdown of attrition rates across departments to identify high-risk areas.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT Department, (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(*)) * 100 AS attrition_rate FROM data GROUP BY Department ORDER BY attrition_rate DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: Comparing attrition across departments is analytically meaningful, and a bar chart effectively highlights differences in categorical data.

kpi_specs.name: Average Monthly Income by Job Role
kpi_specs.description: Average monthly income grouped by job role to assess compensation equity and role valuation.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT JobRole, AVG(MonthlyIncome) AS avg_monthly_income FROM data GROUP BY JobRole ORDER BY avg_monthly_income DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: Compensation equity is a key HR concern. A bar chart allows easy comparison of average income across job roles.

kpi_specs.name: Job Satisfaction Distribution
kpi_specs.description: Count of employees by job satisfaction level (1-4) to gauge overall workforce morale.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT JobSatisfaction, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM data GROUP BY JobSatisfaction ORDER BY JobSatisfaction
kpi_specs.reasoning: Job satisfaction is a critical employee engagement metric. A bar chart effectively displays the distribution of satisfaction levels.

kpi_specs.name: Attrition by Years at Company
kpi_specs.description: Attrition rate segmented by years at the company to identify tenure-related retention risks.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT YearsAtCompany, (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(*)) * 100 AS attrition_rate FROM data GROUP BY YearsAtCompany ORDER BY YearsAtCompany
kpi_specs.reasoning: Analyzing attrition trends over tenure (a continuous variable) is best visualized as a line chart to reveal patterns over time.
